text:
Pradeep: Heads-up — large EU financial customer wants a 2-week POC. Key asks: all inference and KV/cache must stay inside eu-central-1 or an equivalent DE region, BYOK for keys, subprocessor list for auditors, and explicit statement that no inference traffic will egress to the US. They also want a rough cost estimate for ~100M tokens/month and whether Dedicated is required to meet residency.

Jamie: Thanks — can you paste the exact questions from their security team? Also do they require on-prem or is VPC/private hosted ok?

Pradeep: Short excerpt from their questionnaire: "Please list all subprocessors, describe network paths (ingress/egress), KMS model (BYOK/HSM), and any third-country access to data. Provide expected max RPS and storage of logs." They said VPC/private-hosted is fine if we can guarantee no cross-border egress and provide audit logs.

Sarah: For residency: hosted API in eu-central + our EU subprocessor set should cover most asks. But BYOK and guaranteed region tenancy are only offered on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has regional endpoints but we still have control-plane elements in other regions.

Elena: Clarify: our control plane metadata may be routed through our control plane region (currently us-east-1) for hosted customers. That can surface in the questionnaire and usually triggers enterprise objections. Dedicated or Private gives a customer-managed control plane option and can be placed in EU.

Jamie: So short answer to customer: if they need BYOK + no control-plane cross-border, go Dedicated/Private. If they accept control-plane metadata in US, hosted EU endpoints might be acceptable. I can draft two pricing buckets.

Pradeep: They explicitly said "no control-plane metadata leaving EU" in follow-up — so looks like Dedicated/Private. Can someone confirm what subprocessors we list for EU-only Dedicated?

Elena: Current EU subprocessors for Dedicated:
- AWS (eu-central-1)
- Fastpath Networking (EU peering provider)
- Logretention EU partner (for optional long-term audit logs)
We do not include any US-based subprocessors for an EU-dedicated deployment. Note: some third-party libs are used in runtime but are not subprocessors for data handling.

Pradeep: Great. Next: KMS/BYOK options and timeline — can we support customer-managed keys in HSM in EU?

Sarah: Yes for Private and Dedicated with KMS integration. We support customer-provided key material (BYOK) via our KMS integrations. For HSM-backed BYOK we need: KMS ARN, key policy review, and a one-week ops window for provisioning.

Jamie: Pricing question — for 100M tokens/month, give two scenarios: Hosted EU (if allowed, slightly cheaper) vs Dedicated reserved (monthly commit). Ops: what uplift for Dedicated and BYOK?

Elena: Uplift components: dedicated GPU pool costs (depends on model family), reserved capacity multiplier (~3-5x hosted unit price depending on commit), and KMS/HSM integration one-time SOW if HSM. Also enablement (networking, certs) ~2-3 engineer-days.

Pradeep: Customer asked about fallback policy — if we lose eu-central nodes, will traffic failover to other regions (which would break residency)? They want guaranteed regional failover to EU-only regional standby.

Sarah: We can offer EU-only failover with dedicated standby in eu-west-1 or another EU region, but that must be part of commit and adds standby capacity cost. If they refuse standby, we can set hard routing to prevent cross-border failover but that reduces resilience.

Jamie: Action items for POC: 1) Draft answer for security questionnaire (Marta to review legal wording), 2) rough Dedicated pricing for 100M tokens with standby option, 3) ops checklist for BYOK/HSM provisioning and estimated lead times, 4) confirm subprocessor list and write a short attestation for no US egress on control-plane for Private/Dedicated.

Marta (Legal): I can review the questionnaire language. Please send the exact Qs. For attestation: we can produce a signed statement for Dedicated/Private deployments that control-plane and data plane will be hosted in EU subprocessors only. Need SOC/ISO evidence for subprocessors — ops to supply.

Pradeep: Copying their specific Qs below (redacted):
> 1) List all subprocessors and their locations.
> 2) Describe network flow diagrams for PII/inference requests.
> 3) Provide KMS integration docs showing BYOK/HSM options.
> 4) Confirm SLA for regional failover and any cross-border fallback.

Sarah: I'll pull together a network flow blurb and a small ASCII diagram we can paste in the questionnaire.

Jamie: I'll draft two pricing scenarios today and tag ops for capacity numbers. If ops can't confirm numbers, I'll add ranges.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: /ops/tickets/RI-POC-4521 — assigned to @Sarah and @Elena. Please update with KMS ARN and network peering details.

Elena: Ops note: For BYOK with HSM in EU we need customer to provide key material OR a KMS ARN. For HSM-backed customer keys we require a security review and a one-week validation window. Also need to schedule a VPN or AWS PrivateLink peering for the VPC-private option.

Pradeep: Can someone confirm timeline for SOW and provisioning? Customer wants POC start in 3 weeks. Realistic?

Sarah: Tight but doable if legal/ops approve ASAP. SOW draft + KMS onboarding + peering = ~10 business days minimum. If they can accept a limited-scope POC (no HSM initial, use RBAC keys) we can compress to 5 business days.

Jamie: I'll propose a two-phase POC: Phase 1 (5 days): EU-hosted with strict routing + audit logs, no HSM; Phase 2 (after commitment): Dedicated with BYOK/HSM and EU-only failover.

Marta (Legal): Sounds sensible. I'll prepare conservative wording for the questionnaire and the attestation. Send me the subprocessor names and SOC/ISO links.

Pradeep: Thanks — I'll coordinate with customer and come back with their preference on HSM vs temporary RBAC keys.

Jamie: I'll attach the pricing draft here shortly. :thumbsup:
